text: f(R) − f(L − 1); memoised DFS with limit and lead.

Digit DP (数位 DP) counts numbers in [L, R] with a property of their digits. Count f(R) − f(L − 1), where f(N) counts 0 … N. Walk the digits of N from the top with a memoised DFS: state (position, whatever the property needs), plus two flags: limit (all digits so far equal N's, so the next one is capped) and lead (only leading zeros so far).

Memoise only states with limit = false (and lead = false when it matters): those are shared by many prefixes. States with limit = true occur once per position, so they need no memo. Total work: positions × states × 10.

Digit counting (P2602): how many times each digit appears in a … b. All three tests are checked against a Python loop over every number. The memo is cleared for each N because it depends on the target digit only through cnt, but limit-free states are reused within one N.

Windy numbers (P2657): no leading zero, adjacent digits differ by at least 2. The state is just the last digit; while still in leading zeros there is no "last digit", so the difference rule is skipped.
The memo does not depend on N here (only on position and last digit), so it could be kept across calls; clearing it is still the safer habit.
Subset sums one bit at a time.

SOS DP (子集和 DP, sum over subsets): for every mask, g[mask] = Σ f[sub] over all subsets sub of mask. Enumerating subsets costs 3ⁿ (进阶篇第17章); SOS does it in n·2ⁿ by adding one bit at a time: for each bit i, for each mask that has bit i, g[mask] += g[mask without bit i].

After processing bits 0 … i, g[mask] holds the sum over subsets that differ from mask only in bits 0 … i. When all bits are done, that is every subset. The same loop with the condition reversed gives superset sums.
Checked against a direct Python sum over all subsets for random values on 4 bits. With n = 20 this is 2·10⁷ steps instead of 3²⁰ ≈ 3.5·10⁹.
Uses: for each number, does some other number share no bit with it (look up the complement's subsets); counting pairs with AND = 0; inclusion-exclusion over masks done for all masks at once.
Loop order matters: bits outside, masks inside. Swapping them counts some subsets several times.
